PullRequest.Title: build: align telemetry validation across CI and official builds
PullRequest.Body:
Refs #336369. Follow-up to #336747 and #336857.

## Problem

[PR #336704's passing metadata job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35376953735/job/105703767426) executed extractor **1.14.0**, while official builds now use **1.20.5**. The Copilot PR gate independently pinned **1.20.4**, and its official packaging step requested an unversioned extractor and ignored nonzero exit codes.

Updating the version alone also exposes two issues: the general gate combines unrelated core/extension namespaces, and Copilot has conflicting descriptions for the same `copilotcloud.chat.sessionCreate.durationMs` property.

## Changes

- Resolve every standalone extractor invocation from the **exact root lockfile version**, so future package updates reach the PR gates and official builds together.
- Run the general PR gate through the **existing official core/extension extraction script**, preserving its separate scopes, prefixes, endpoint handling and validation. Use the repository Node version and install only the extractor outside the checkout; no full VS Code dependency install is needed.
- Keep Copilot validation separate and make the official Copilot extraction step propagate validation failures.
- Give success/failure declarations of the cloud-session duration property one compatible description. Emitted events, fields, classifications and runtime behavior are unchanged.

The official build's existing heap setting remains unchanged. No validation is disabled.

## Validation

Ran the actual updated YAML commands locally on Node 24.18.0 / Windows with Git Bash, using the published 1.20.5 package and no repository dependencies installed:

| Path | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Locked extractor installation | Pass |
| Shared official core + extension extraction | Pass: 486 core events / 34 common properties; 72 built-in/helper events / 14 common properties |
| Copilot PR validation | Pass |
| Copilot official extraction | Pass: 240 events / 4 common properties |

- Confirmed 1.14.0 accepts the invalid first-response/common-session-property fixture, while 1.20.5 rejects it; both accept the corrected fixture.
- Focused TypeScript compilation, YAML parsing, targeted hygiene and `git diff --check` pass.
- The Copilot metadata correction produces identical runtime JavaScript with comments removed.

This branch includes the merged #336857 fix. These are local execution results, not a claim that remote CI has completed; no manual CI/Azure rerun or infrastructure change was requested.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The pull_request trigger, synchronous clone path, and fixed six-clone cardinality are explicit. The extraction config and repository search also prove that vscode-node-debug2 is not consumed; only network-dependent duration is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one external Git clone plus its downloaded bytes and checkout writes per run
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One unused clone is paid on every PR run and rerun; all six clones execute serially before validation starts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased CI latency and unnecessary network/filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The workflow directly ran the extractor on the checked-out repository and performed no Git clones.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each PR metadata job now enters a synchronous loop that shallow-clones six external repositories before extraction.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 31 replaces the direct extractor command with `node build/azure-pipelines/common/extract-telemetry.ts`, newly executing that script's clone loop in every PR metadata job.
Findings.Title: Skip the unused clone added to every metadata check
Findings.Impact: Every PR to main or a release branch waits for an unnecessary cold repository download and checkout before telemetry validation, increasing required-check latency and network usage.
Findings.Evidence: The invoked script synchronously runs `git clone --depth 1` for six repositories. One is vscode-node-debug2, while telemetry-config.json references vscode-chrome-debug-core and vscode-node-debug but never vscode-node-debug2, so that checkout cannot contribute to either extractor output.
Findings.Recommendation: Remove vscode-node-debug2 from the shared clone list, or derive clones from configured source directories, preserving extraction output while eliminating the unused boundary call.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: After checkout and Node setup, the job must install the extractor, run the shared script, complete all six serial repository clones, and finish two serial extractor subprocesses before the required metadata check can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the lockfile-selected telemetry extractor and dependencies from npm into runner temp.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install per workflow run on a fresh GitHub-hosted runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old npx command also had to resolve/download the pinned extractor when absent, so this is mainly a relocation rather than proven extra boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks extraction; effectively cold because no dependency cache is configured for the temporary prefix.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six sequential clones per PR run; five repositories are named by telemetry configuration and vscode-node-debug2 is not referenced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior workflow invoked the extractor directly over the checkout and cloned zero repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All clones finish before either extractor starts; the unused clone contributes pure latency and I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run telemetry extraction once for core and once for configured extensions/helper repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two serial Node subprocesses per run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One npx-launched extractor invocation scanned the checked-out repository.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One execution for every pull request targeting main or release branches and every rerun; within each run the external-repository cardinality is fixed at six and is not cached or grouped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The npm install is followed by six synchronous `execSync` clones and then two synchronous `execSync` Node extractor calls; there is no overlap, limiter, or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub-hosted runners and RUNNER_TEMP are fresh; no npm or Git cache is configured. The extractor install and six checkouts are cold each run.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed workflow directly invokes a script whose synchronous clone loop is explicit, and configuration/search prove one cloned repository is unused.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact clone and extraction duration varies with repository size, network, and runner load; the unused clone and its placement on the critical path are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity boundary fan-out: the new path adds six cold serial clones, including one that cannot affect output and can be removed without changing validation.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout and Node setup precede a single npx telemetry-extractor invocation; that invocation must complete for the check to pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/install the exact lockfile-selected extractor through npx when it is not locally cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one package resolution/install per Copilot telemetry job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old command made the same npx boundary call with version 1.20.4; only version sourcing changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the telemetry check on cold resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan the Copilot extension with vscode-telemetry-extractor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One equivalent extractor invocation ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the validation itself and blocks completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Copilot source size and telemetry declaration count; one invocation per PR job.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One foreground npx/extractor process; no per-event subprocess fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: npx may reuse an available package cache, but no new cache behavior or key was introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that command cardinality and scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The performance difference between extractor versions 1.20.4 and 1.20.5 is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; version lookup is trivial and boundary cardinality is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Official Copilot extension build and packaging
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After setup/build/l10n, telemetry extraction runs synchronously before JSON minification and VSIX packaging.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the lockfile-selected extractor through npx if unavailable locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One npx package request per official Copilot job, subject to existing local npm state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous unversioned npx invocation had the same potential package-resolution boundary.
One synchronous spawn ran before; the change makes exit status authoritative and pins the package version.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Copilot extension source size; one extraction per build.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One foreground npx/extractor child process; failure now propagates, but no extra process is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Can reuse dependencies prepared by existing Copilot setup steps; the diff does not add retained caches or alter cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that subprocess count remains one.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Any runtime delta from selecting 1.20.5 rather than whichever unversioned package npx resolved is unmeasured and unsupported as a regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Official core and built-in extension telemetry generation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Compilation is followed by the existing shared extraction script; its clones and two extractor calls remain on the same official-build path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone helper repositories used by the shared official extraction script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six shallow clones per official extraction, unchanged by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same script and clone loop already ran in Linux x64, macOS, and Windows official build definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks official telemetry generation as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same invocations using the root node_modules extractor path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Core source, selected built-in extensions, and fixed helper-repository set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Six serial clones and two serial extractor calls, unchanged for official builds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache logic changed. When VSCODE_TELEMETRY_EXTRACTOR is unset, the existing root node_modules path remains in use.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: nullish fallback preserves the exact prior path for official callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for causality; the environment override is inactive on these existing callers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new official-build performance regression from the environment override.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cloud session success/failure sends the same telemetry event and measurement as before.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cloud session creation attempts, but emitted payload fields and frequency are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scheduling, allocation, or boundary behavior changes; only metadata comments changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved or changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: executable telemetry calls are byte-for-byte unchanged in the shown hunks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None; the diff changes comments only.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced PR validation, official-build extraction, Copilot packaging, and runtime telemetry paths. One low-severity boundary-fan-out issue was submitted for the newly reached, provably unused cold Git clone; no other changed mechanism established a performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
